paragraphs.title: The Miracles of the Exodus and Understanding Them

easy.question: Whom did Moses call at the beginning of the passage?
answers: All Israel
Pharaoh
The servants of Egypt
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “Moses called unto all Israel.”

easy.question: In which land did the Lord do the things Israel saw?
answers: The wilderness
The land of Egypt
The land of Canaan
easy.explanation: Moses recalls all that the Lord did before Israel’s eyes in the land of Egypt.

easy.question: What did the Israelites see in Egypt?
answers: Only Pharaoh’s palace
Only the wilderness
Great temptations, signs, and miracles
easy.explanation: The verses mention great temptations, signs, and great miracles.

medium.question: For whom were the deeds that the Lord did in Egypt performed, according to Moses?
answers: Pharaoh, his servants, and all his land
Moses alone
Only the Israelites in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The verse specifically mentions Pharaoh, all his servants, and all his land.

medium.question: What does “miracles” mean in the phrase “signs and great miracles”?
answers: Simple laws
Wonders or extraordinary acts
Places to live
medium.explanation: In this context, miracles are wondrous or extraordinary acts.

medium.question: What is the connection between seeing the miracles and the third verse?
answers: Everyone who saw the miracles immediately understood everything
The miracles happened only after Israel entered the land
Although Israel saw them, the people still had not been given an understanding heart
medium.explanation: Israel saw the great deeds, but the verse says they still had not been given a heart to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear.

challenge.question: What central idea emerges from the contrast between verses 2 and 3?
answers: People can see great events and still fail to understand their meaning
Israel did not see the events of Egypt at all
The signs and miracles were ordinary events
challenge.explanation: Israel saw the signs and miracles, yet they were not given a heart to understand; seeing does not guarantee understanding.

challenge.question: Why does Moses mention Pharaoh, his servants, and all his land together?
answers: To describe only Pharaoh’s family
To emphasize that the deeds affected all Egypt, from its ruler to the land
To say that Pharaoh helped Israel
challenge.explanation: The list expands the description from Pharaoh and his servants to the whole land, emphasizing the scope of the deeds.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “unto this day” at the end of the passage?
answers: The words were spoken only at the time of the Exodus
Moses is speaking about an event far in the future
Even after many years, the people’s lack of understanding had not completely changed
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the lack of understanding continued until Moses’ time, rather than being limited to a brief moment in the past.

questions.question: What central idea emerges from the contrast between verses 2 and 3?
answers: People can see great events and still fail to understand their meaning
Israel did not see the events of Egypt at all
The signs and miracles were ordinary events
questions.explanation: Israel saw the signs and miracles, yet they were not given a heart to understand; seeing does not guarantee understanding.

questions.question: Why does Moses mention Pharaoh, his servants, and all his land together?
answers: To describe only Pharaoh’s family
To emphasize that the deeds affected all Egypt, from its ruler to the land
To say that Pharaoh helped Israel
questions.explanation: The list expands the description from Pharaoh and his servants to the whole land, emphasizing the scope of the deeds.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “unto this day” at the end of the passage?
answers: The words were spoken only at the time of the Exodus
Moses is speaking about an event far in the future
Even after many years, the people’s lack of understanding had not completely changed
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that the lack of understanding continued until Moses’ time, rather than being limited to a brief moment in the past.

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Care for Israel in the Wilderness and Their Victories

easy.question: How many years did the Lord lead the people in the wilderness?
answers: Forty years
Seven years
One hundred years
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I have led you forty years in the wilderness.”

easy.question: What did not wear out during the wilderness years?
answers: The food and water
The clothes and shoes
The houses and tents
easy.explanation: The verse says that the clothes did not wear out and the shoes did not wear out on their feet.

easy.question: Who came out to fight against Israel?
answers: Pharaoh and Egypt
Amalek and Moab
Sihon and Og
easy.explanation: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against Israel in battle.

medium.question: Why did Israel not eat bread or drink wine or strong drink in the wilderness?
answers: So that they would know that the Lord was their God
Because they had no time to eat
Because they had already reached the land
medium.explanation: The verse says this was so they would know that the Lord was their God.

medium.question: What did the Israelites do after defeating Sihon and Og?
answers: They immediately returned to the wilderness
They took their land and gave it as an inheritance
They built a temple for themselves
medium.explanation: After the victory, Israel took the land and gave it to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

medium.question: In the phrase “wine or strong drink,” what does “strong drink” mean?
answers: Payment for work
Sweet water
An intoxicating beverage
medium.explanation: The phrase concerns drinking and places strong drink alongside wine, so it means an intoxicating beverage.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the clothes and shoes did not wear out during forty years in the wilderness?
answers: The Lord cared for the people’s needs and sustained them in a special way
The people did not travel in the wilderness at all
The clothes and shoes were made of stone
challenge.explanation: This detail emphasizes the Lord’s protection and care for the people over a long period in the wilderness.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the victories, the inherited land, and the last verse?
answers: The victories removed the need for the covenant
The blessings and successes required Israel to keep the words of the covenant
The land was given only to those who drank wine
challenge.explanation: After describing the Lord’s help and Israel’s success, the people are told to keep and obey the covenant so that they may prosper in all they do.

challenge.question: Which specific detail about the distribution of the land appears in these verses?
answers: All the land was given to the tribe of Judah
The land was divided equally among all twelve tribes
The land was given to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the inheritance was given to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the clothes and shoes did not wear out during forty years in the wilderness?
answers: The Lord cared for the people’s needs and sustained them in a special way
The people did not travel in the wilderness at all
The clothes and shoes were made of stone
questions.explanation: This detail emphasizes the Lord’s protection and care for the people over a long period in the wilderness.

questions.question: What is the connection between the victories, the inherited land, and the last verse?
answers: The victories removed the need for the covenant
The blessings and successes required Israel to keep the words of the covenant
The land was given only to those who drank wine
questions.explanation: After describing the Lord’s help and Israel’s success, the people are told to keep and obey the covenant so that they may prosper in all they do.

questions.question: Which specific detail about the distribution of the land appears in these verses?
answers: All the land was given to the tribe of Judah
The land was divided equally among all twelve tribes
The land was given to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the inheritance was given to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

paragraphs.title: All the People Enter the Covenant

easy.question: Before whom do all the Israelites stand?
answers: Before Pharaoh
Before the Lord their God
Before the king of Moab
easy.explanation: The verse says, “You stand this day all of you before the Lord your God.”

easy.question: Who was included among those entering the covenant?
answers: Only the elders
Only the priests
All the people, including women, children, and foreigners
easy.explanation: The verses mention leaders, elders, officers, women, children, foreigners, and all the men of Israel.

easy.question: Why does the people enter into a covenant with the Lord?
answers: So that they will be his people and he will be their God
To choose a new king
To return to Egypt
easy.explanation: The covenant establishes Israel as the Lord’s people, with the Lord as their God.

medium.question: Why are people from every part of the nation mentioned, from the leaders to the woodcutters and water drawers?
answers: To show that the covenant binds the entire people
To describe construction work only
To distinguish Israel from the nations
medium.explanation: The list emphasizes that the covenant is not only for leaders but for every level of the people.

medium.question: In the phrase “your stranger that is in your camp,” what does “stranger” mean?
answers: Your enemy
A foreign resident living among you
Your tribal leader
medium.explanation: The context says that the stranger is in Israel’s camp, meaning a foreign resident living among the people.

medium.question: How do verses 12–13 relate to verse 11?
answers: Verse 11 describes the people present, while verses 12–13 explain the covenant’s purpose and scope
Verse 11 cancels the covenant, while verses 12–13 propose a new one
Verse 11 concerns Egypt, while verses 12–13 concern a war
medium.explanation: Verse 11 lists those present, and the following verses explain that the covenant makes them the Lord’s people and includes those not physically present.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the mention of someone who is not present at the covenant ceremony?
answers: The covenant belongs only to the wilderness generation
The covenant also binds future generations
Those who are absent are exempt from every obligation
challenge.explanation: The passage says the covenant includes those who are not there that day, pointing to future generations.

challenge.question: What does the word “all” emphasize at the beginning of the passage?
answers: Only a small group of leaders is participating
The whole people are together, with all their classes and parts
Only those who left Egypt may participate
challenge.explanation: The word is explained by the following list: leaders, elders, officers, women, children, foreigners, and workers.

challenge.question: Why does Moses mention both Egypt and the journey among the nations?
answers: To recall the journey and experiences that brought the people to the covenant
To announce that the people are returning to live in Egypt
To describe only the place where the Law was given
challenge.explanation: Mentioning Egypt and the journey among the nations reminds the people of their past and the path they traveled before entering the covenant.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the mention of someone who is not present at the covenant ceremony?
answers: The covenant belongs only to the wilderness generation
The covenant also binds future generations
Those who are absent are exempt from every obligation
questions.explanation: The passage says the covenant includes those who are not there that day, pointing to future generations.

questions.question: What does the word “all” emphasize at the beginning of the passage?
answers: Only a small group of leaders is participating
The whole people are together, with all their classes and parts
Only those who left Egypt may participate
questions.explanation: The word is explained by the following list: leaders, elders, officers, women, children, foreigners, and workers.

questions.question: Why does Moses mention both Egypt and the journey among the nations?
answers: To recall the journey and experiences that brought the people to the covenant
To announce that the people are returning to live in Egypt
To describe only the place where the Law was given
questions.explanation: Mentioning Egypt and the journey among the nations reminds the people of their past and the path they traveled before entering the covenant.

paragraphs.title: Warning Against Idolatry and a Wicked Root

easy.question: What did the Israelites see among the nations?
answers: Idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold
Scrolls of the Law and lamps
Houses, fields, and wells
easy.explanation: The passage says they saw idols made of wood, stone, silver, and gold.

easy.question: Who might turn to worship the gods of the nations?
answers: Only the king of Israel
A man, woman, family, or tribe
Only the priests
easy.explanation: The passage warns that an individual, woman, family, or tribe might turn away from the Lord.

easy.question: What did the person say in his heart despite hearing the words of the curse?
answers: I must repent
I have nothing to fear
I shall have peace
easy.explanation: He said in his heart, “I shall have peace,” even though he intended to follow his stubborn heart.

medium.question: What sin is described in the person who says, “I shall have peace”?
answers: He thinks he can sin as he pleases without punishment
He fears punishment and runs away
He immediately asks for forgiveness
medium.explanation: He reassures himself that he will have peace even while continuing in the stubbornness of his heart.

medium.question: In the phrase “to add drunkenness to thirst,” what idea is expressed?
answers: Separating two things
Adding or joining one thing to another
Hiding something
medium.explanation: The phrase describes adding drunkenness to thirst—that is, joining a harmful excess to an existing desire.

medium.question: What is described as happening to this person in verses 19–20?
answers: He becomes a leader over Israel
He receives a special blessing
The curse rests on him, his name is blotted out, and he is set apart for evil
medium.explanation: The verses describe the Lord’s anger, the curses resting on him, his name being blotted out, and his separation from Israel for evil.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “a root that bears gall and wormwood” symbolize in this chapter?
answers: A hidden source that may produce sin and harmful influence
A tree used to make medicine
A root that provides food for the whole nation
challenge.explanation: The image describes a person or group whose tendency toward idolatry may spread and harm others.

challenge.question: Why is the punishment especially severe according to the passage?
answers: Because the person never heard the words of the Law
Because he heard the curse but still trusted his stubborn heart
Because he was punished for an accidental mistake
challenge.explanation: He heard the words of the curse but still said in his heart that he would have peace and continued in his own way.

challenge.question: What important detail can be inferred from the punishment in verse 20?
answers: The punishment affects only his property
The punishment ends with a private apology
He is separated for evil from all the tribes of Israel, not merely punished as an individual
challenge.explanation: The verse says the Lord will separate him for evil from all the tribes of Israel, involving exclusion from the community as well as personal punishment.

questions.question: What does the phrase “a root that bears gall and wormwood” symbolize in this chapter?
answers: A hidden source that may produce sin and harmful influence
A tree used to make medicine
A root that provides food for the whole nation
questions.explanation: The image describes a person or group whose tendency toward idolatry may spread and harm others.

questions.question: Why is the punishment especially severe according to the passage?
answers: Because the person never heard the words of the Law
Because he heard the curse but still trusted his stubborn heart
Because he was punished for an accidental mistake
questions.explanation: He heard the words of the curse but still said in his heart that he would have peace and continued in his own way.

questions.question: What important detail can be inferred from the punishment in verse 20?
answers: The punishment affects only his property
The punishment ends with a private apology
He is separated for evil from all the tribes of Israel, not merely punished as an individual
questions.explanation: The verse says the Lord will separate him for evil from all the tribes of Israel, involving exclusion from the community as well as personal punishment.

paragraphs.title: The Desolation of the Land and the Question of Future Generations

easy.question: Who will see the plagues of the land?
answers: The future generation and the foreigner
Only the priests
Only the kings of the nations
easy.explanation: The passage says that the future generation and a foreigner from a distant land will see the land’s plagues.

easy.question: What will happen to the land?
answers: It will be full of trees
It will not be sown and will produce nothing
It will have flourishing fields
easy.explanation: The land is described as a place that cannot be sown and where no plants grow.

easy.question: Who will ask, “Why has the Lord done this to this land?”
answers: The Israelites alone
The foreigners alone
All the nations
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Even all nations shall say.”

medium.question: What is the order of events described in the passage?
answers: People see the ruined land and then ask why it was treated this way
People ask why, and then the land begins to flourish
The land is sown, and then the nations arrive
medium.explanation: First the people see the land’s plagues and desolation; afterward they ask why this happened.

medium.question: What caused the land’s severe desolation?
answers: A great storm
The Lord’s anger and wrath
A war among the nations
medium.explanation: The passage explains that the destruction resulted from the Lord’s anger and wrath.

medium.question: In the phrase “the sicknesses which the Lord hath laid upon it,” what does “sicknesses” refer to?
answers: Its crops
Its borders
Its afflictions or plagues
medium.explanation: The context of the land’s plagues shows that these are severe afflictions or calamities laid upon the land.

challenge.question: Why is the land compared to the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah?
answers: To emphasize that the destruction was extreme and complete
To teach that the land was a city in Sodom
To show that the land became fertile
challenge.explanation: The comparison to Sodom and Gomorrah emphasizes the extent of the destruction and the land’s terrible desolation.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the mention of “the stranger that shall come from a far land”?
answers: Only someone who lives in the land can understand its destruction
Even an outsider will notice the destruction and ask why it happened
The stranger caused the destruction
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that even a foreigner from far away will see the ruined land and wonder about its cause.

challenge.question: What do the details “brimstone and salt” and “no grass grows there” show together?
answers: The land is especially suitable for farming
The land was burned only briefly
The land became desolate and difficult to cultivate
challenge.explanation: Brimstone, salt, and the absence of vegetation point to deep destruction that made the land barren.

questions.question: Why is the land compared to the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah?
answers: To emphasize that the destruction was extreme and complete
To teach that the land was a city in Sodom
To show that the land became fertile
questions.explanation: The comparison to Sodom and Gomorrah emphasizes the extent of the destruction and the land’s terrible desolation.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the mention of “the stranger that shall come from a far land”?
answers: Only someone who lives in the land can understand its destruction
Even an outsider will notice the destruction and ask why it happened
The stranger caused the destruction
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that even a foreigner from far away will see the ruined land and wonder about its cause.

questions.question: What do the details “brimstone and salt” and “no grass grows there” show together?
answers: The land is especially suitable for farming
The land was burned only briefly
The land became desolate and difficult to cultivate
questions.explanation: Brimstone, salt, and the absence of vegetation point to deep destruction that made the land barren.

paragraphs.title: Abandoning the Covenant, Exile, and Responsibility to the Law

easy.question: What did the Israelites forsake, according to the passage?
answers: The covenant of the Lord
The land of Egypt
The book of the Law
easy.explanation: The passage says that they forsook the covenant of the Lord made with their ancestors.

easy.question: Whom did the Israelites serve and worship?
answers: Moses
Other gods
The kings of the land
easy.explanation: The passage says that they served other gods and worshiped them.

easy.question: What did the Lord do to Israel because of its sin?
answers: He returned them to Egypt
He gave them another land
He drove them out into another land
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord rooted them out of their land and cast them into another land.

medium.question: Why was the Lord’s anger kindled against the land?
answers: Because the people served other gods and forsook his covenant
Because they did not build cities
Because they wanted to move to another land
medium.explanation: Forsaking the covenant and serving other gods caused the Lord’s anger and brought the curses upon the land.

medium.question: In the phrase “the Lord rooted them out of their land,” what does “rooted them out” mean?
answers: Praised them
Uprooted or removed them from their place
Called them to return
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the Lord uprooted or removed them from their land.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in the passage?
answers: Exile, idolatry, the Lord’s anger, and abandoning the covenant
The Lord’s anger, keeping the Law, idolatry, and exile
Abandoning the covenant, idolatry, the Lord’s anger, and exile
medium.explanation: First they abandoned the covenant, then served other gods; as a result, the Lord became angry and exiled them.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the phrase “gods whom they knew not, and whom he had not given unto them”?
answers: These were not gods given to or recognized by Israel
The people knew the other gods very well
The people received these gods at Mount Sinai
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that these were gods Israel did not know and had not been given to worship.

challenge.question: What does the ending “the secret things belong unto the Lord... but the things which are revealed belong unto us” teach?
answers: There is no need to keep the Law
People must obey what has been revealed to them, even if some things remain hidden
All secrets have been revealed to everyone
challenge.explanation: The verse distinguishes between hidden things that belong to the Lord and revealed things that people are responsible to obey.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “for ever” refer to at the end of the verse?
answers: The length of time they will remain in exile
The duration of the Lord’s anger alone
The continuing obligation to do all the words of the Law
challenge.explanation: The phrase is connected with doing all the words of the Law and emphasizes the lasting duty to obey it.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the phrase “gods whom they knew not, and whom he had not given unto them”?
answers: These were not gods given to or recognized by Israel
The people knew the other gods very well
The people received these gods at Mount Sinai
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that these were gods Israel did not know and had not been given to worship.

questions.question: What does the ending “the secret things belong unto the Lord... but the things which are revealed belong unto us” teach?
answers: There is no need to keep the Law
People must obey what has been revealed to them, even if some things remain hidden
All secrets have been revealed to everyone
questions.explanation: The verse distinguishes between hidden things that belong to the Lord and revealed things that people are responsible to obey.

questions.question: What does the phrase “for ever” refer to at the end of the verse?
answers: The length of time they will remain in exile
The duration of the Lord’s anger alone
The continuing obligation to do all the words of the Law
questions.explanation: The phrase is connected with doing all the words of the Law and emphasizes the lasting duty to obey it.
